public_rationale: Zitron's claim is hedged: concentration 'appears' to be worsening, and he grounds it in bank projections. Reports say Barclays sees the two labs' share of AWS revenue rising from 13% to 18%, and UBS sees their share of Google Cloud rising from 27% to 48%. But these figures reach the public only through his own work. They are also forecasts for 2027, not shares anyone has observed. Microsoft's figures suggest OpenAI grew to about a third of its backlog in FY2026. That points the same way, but it is backlog, not revenue, and covers one company. No hyperscaler reports revenue by customer. So the independent record neither confirms nor refutes the trend.
limitations: Analyst notes are paywalled. I relied on secondary reports.
Backlog share is a different metric from revenue share.

our_interpretation: The claim is hedged ('appears'). I read it as: the analyst estimates and other public evidence available by the post date show OpenAI and Anthropic taking a rising share of hyperscaler (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) AI or cloud revenue over successive periods.
I do not treat it as a firm claim of a measured trend. A hedged 'appears' is tested against what the public record showed, not held to a definite audited trend.
No period is named. I take the period to run from 2025 through the post date (2026-08-11), covering the latest reported quarter (Q2 calendar 2026) and the analyst notes then in circulation.
Hyperscalers do not disclose revenue by customer, so the test must rest on independent analyst estimates or company disclosures, not on the speaker's own compilation.
criteria.support_condition: Independent, citable analyst estimates or company disclosures, published by the evaluation date, showing OpenAI and Anthropic's share of hyperscaler AI or cloud revenue rising from one period to the next.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent analyst estimates or company disclosures showing that share flat or falling across successive periods, or showing non-lab customers growing faster than the two labs.
